Read 0 Hz f0 values as missing

Source: R/resample.R
zero_hz_to_na.Rd

Pitch trackers write 0 Hz for unvoiced frames, where no pitch was measured. A 0 left in the data is read as a very low pitch: it pulls mean contours and fits towards 0, and gives -Inf in semitones. This sets 0 to NA in the f0 columns of df. The app does this to every CSV uploaded in the Start tab.

Usage

zero_hz_to_na(df, cols = hz_f0_columns(df))

Arguments

df

A data frame.

cols

Names of the columns to clean. Defaults to the f0 columns found as described in Details.

Value

df with 0 set to NA in cols. Attribute "zero_hz" gives the number of values changed, named by column, for the columns with at least one; it is an empty integer vector when there were none.

Details

By default the f0 columns are found by name and by value. A column is used when:

  • its name has the word f0, pitch or hz, or one of VoiceSauce's f0 names (strF0, sF0, pF0, shrF0, oF0), and its other words are ones that keep the values in Hz: raw, corrected, original, edited, smoothed, interp, praat, reaper, mean, median, max, min, peak and the like, or a number. So f0, F0_Hz, pitch, f0_corrected and mean_f0 are used, but not f0_st, f0_dur, f0_peak_loc or pitch_rank, where 0 is a real value. Words are split at any character other than a letter or digit;

  • it is numeric with no negative values, so a normalised column (which has negatives) is never touched;

  • the median of its positive values lies between 30 and 2000, a plausible range for f0 in Hz.

Negative values, which some trackers use for unvoiced frames, are left as they are, and a column that has any is not used. Give cols to choose the columns yourself.

See also

normalise_f0(), which also reads f0 of 0 or below as NA.

Examples

df <- data.frame(token = "ma1", time = 1:5 / 100,
                 f0 = c(0, 212, 215, 0, 210),
                 intensity = c(0, 68, 70, 66, 0))
out <- zero_hz_to_na(df)
out$f0          # NA where the tracker wrote 0
#> [1]  NA 212 215  NA 210
out$intensity   # unchanged
#> [1]  0 68 70 66  0
attr(out, "zero_hz")
#> f0 
#>  2
